key_highlights: Iron ore crash confirmed, pressuring BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX and materials sector broadly
ASX edged higher on the day but 'stock shock builds' signals rising volatility ahead of Fed meeting
Oil spike and 30c fuel price rise in Australia weigh on consumer and transport sectors
ANZ.AX post-3,500-job-cut restructuring still faces execution risk
WA gold exploration activity (Forrestania, PLC Resources) supports junior miners
Nvidia 2GW Australia AI data-centre push signals long-term tech infrastructure demand
Housing market soft: no auction bounce, falling prices, REIT pressure
Major private hospital operator breakup signals healthcare sector consolidation
China geopolitical pivot and Arctic shipping route shift add commodity trade uncertainty
Immigration policy overhaul debate impacts labour supply and productivity narrative

sectors.trend: Iron ore crash in progress; China demand concerns and geopolitical pivot weigh on pricing. Gold exploration in WA (Forrestania 2Mt deal, PLC Resources) provides a relative bright spot. Junior miners (PolarX, Sunstone, Manuka) showing momentum.
sectors.implications: BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX face margin compression. Gold juniors (PLC.AX, FOR.AX) and diversified miners with gold exposure offer relative strength. Monitor iron ore contract pricing weekly.

sectors.trend: ANZ.AX restructuring after 3,500 job cuts still in execution phase. Superannuation system under scrutiny. Housing weakness pressures mortgage growth and NIM. Fed meeting adds rate-path uncertainty.
sectors.implications: Big Four (CBA.AX, ANZ.AX, NAB.AX, WBC.AX) face mixed signals: cost discipline vs. credit risk from housing. Super fund flows may shift if reform debate gains traction.

sectors.trend: Australia nearing energy inflection point; oil spike and 30c fuel price rise. Whyalla steelworks job losses signal industrial energy demand softening. LNG and renewables transition accelerating.
sectors.implications: Woodside (WDS.AX), Santos (STO.AX) benefit from oil strength. Coal and industrial energy names face demand headwinds. Renewables and grid infrastructure names gain policy tailwind.

sectors.trend: Major private hospital operator breakup via lender-backed consortium signals sector consolidation. CSL.AX remains defensive anchor. Bird flu in SA (pelican, sea lion) adds biosecurity risk.
sectors.implications: Healthcare REITs and hospital operators face M&A disruption. CSL.AX, SGH.AX offer defensive positioning. Biosecurity concerns could impact agricultural-linked health names.

sectors.trend: Nvidia 2GW Australia AI data-centre push, Google $200B AI capex, and AI slowdown debate create a bifurcated narrative. ASX small-caps (Neurizon, Iondrive) gaining attention.
sectors.implications: Australian data-centre and power infrastructure names benefit. ASX-listed tech remains thin; exposure via global tech (NVDA, GOOGL) and local enablers (VIX.AX, IAG.AX).

sectors.trend: Fuel price rise and oil spike pressure Qantas (QAN.AX) and consumer discretionary. One-in-three flight cancellations due to staff shortages. Housing affordability debate suppresses consumer confidence.
sectors.implications: QAN.AX, WES.AX, WOW.AX face margin pressure. Defensive consumer staples (WES.AX, WOL.AX) preferred. Housing-linked retail (SGH.AX, LPX.AX) under pressure.

key_themes: Iron ore crash and China demand uncertainty dominate materials
Energy transition inflection with oil spike vs. renewables policy
Housing market correction pressuring banks, REITs, and consumer
AI infrastructure build-out in Australia (Nvidia, Google)
Immigration policy overhaul and productivity debate
Geopolitical risk: China pivot, Arctic shipping, US-Iran tensions

risk_assessment.mitigation: Reduce BHP.AX/RIO.AX/FMG.AX exposure; rotate into gold and diversified miners; hedge with commodity futures
Underweight REITs and housing-linked financials; favour defensive dividend payers; monitor RBA policy response
Hedge transport and consumer exposure; favour energy producers (WDS.AX, STO.AX); monitor AUD/USD
Maintain 15-20% cash allocation; diversify into gold (GOLD.AX, NGT.AX); avoid single-country concentration
Monitor labour-intensive sectors (construction, hospitality); favour automation/AI beneficiaries
Track ANZ.AX cost-out progress; favour CBA.AX and NAB.AX with cleaner balance sheets

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gold miners and exploration names
opportunities.rationale: Iron ore crash rotates capital into gold; WA exploration pipeline (Forrestania, PLC) active; geopolitical hedge

opportunities.recommendation: Add energy producers on oil spike
opportunities.rationale: 30c fuel rise and oil strength support WDS.AX, STO.AX margins; energy inflection point supports structural demand
Nvidia 2GW Australia push and Google $200B capex drive power, data-centre, and grid demand in Australia
Private hospital operator breakup creates consolidation opportunities; CSL.AX remains defensive anchor

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce iron ore and China-exposed materials
defensive_moves.rationale: Iron ore crash confirmed; China demand pivot and Arctic shipping shift threaten volumes
No auction bounce, falling prices, and credit risk build; RBA may need to cut, compressing NIMs
Fuel spike, flight cancellations, and weak consumer confidence pressure QAN.AX and retail
Stock shock building, Fed meeting uncertainty, and geopolitical risks warrant liquidity buffer

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely range-bound to slightly lower over 1-3 months. Iron ore crash and oil spike create sector divergence. Fed meeting and RBA policy path are key swing factors. Volatility elevated ('stock shock builds'). Expect materials to underperform while energy and gold outperform.
market_outlook.long_term: 6-12 month outlook cautiously constructive if iron ore stabilises and energy transition accelerates. AI infrastructure capex in Australia provides a structural growth vector. Housing correction may force RBA cuts, supporting rate-sensitive sectors. Immigration policy overhaul could boost productivity narrative. Key risk: China demand collapse extending iron ore weakness.
